analysis.answer: Currently, no law addresses religious displays in public school classrooms. This measure mandates that every public school classroom display a specific religious poster of the Five Pillars of Islam.

Direct costs include printing, distributing, and potentially framing at least one 11 by 14 inch poster for every public school classroom in the jurisdiction. There may also be litigation costs associated with defending the mandate.
Taxpayers or local school districts would bear the costs of acquiring and maintaining the posters. Students, teachers, and school staff are the primary audience who will interact with the displays.

The measure is highly likely to trigger First Amendment litigation regarding the Establishment Clause. School administrators will have to monitor classrooms for compliance, while some teachers or parents may protest or refuse to comply.
The text asserts a requirement for a religious display without stating the underlying problem it aims to address.
The state legislature gains direct control over classroom wall displays, reducing the discretion previously held by local school boards, school administrators, and individual teachers.
This is a statutory requirement that could be repealed by future legislation or struck down by courts.
